text:
Alex Nedeljkovic made 24 saves on a night when SJS was handed chances worth 3.76 expected goals, and that goalie work is the cleanest explanation for how San Jose walked out of Enterprise Center with a win. STL generated more of everything, including 56 shot attempts to 51 and a 63 percent share of simulated replays, but Nedeljkovic saved 1.76 goals more than the shots he faced should have cost him.

The first period was all STL, 1.75 expected goals to 0.40. Connor McMichael's tip-in at 3:52 made it 1-0, and Mason McTavish had a 43 percent look stopped by Nedeljkovic. San Jose pulled even when Tyler Toffoli scored at 8:48 of the second, and the shot quality tilted its way from there. Dillon Dube put STL ahead short-handed early in the third from a 9 percent chance, the sort of goal that rarely repeats. Collin Graf answered at 6:05 with a snap shot, a 32 percent chance, and the game was tied again.

Overtime lasted 1:03. Darnell Nurse beat Joel Hofer with a wrist shot, assisted by Ivar Stenberg and Alexander Wennberg, to make it SJS 3, STL 2. Neither team scored on the power play (SJS 0 for 4, STL 0 for 2), so the decision came at even strength. Toffoli, with a goal and an assist, was named the first star.
